header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Time: 16:00 - 16:58 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: All-hands (Zoom)
Host: Maya Chen (CEO)
Attendees: ~150 (recording includes leadership plus cross-functional updates)
summary: Leadership updates across product, engineering, research, sales, security, and people. Major announcements: Dedicated v2 pilot start, Q4 hiring plan adjustments, SOC2 progress, and updated OKRs. Open Q&A at the end; several follow-ups assigned.
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: All right hi everyone thanks for joining on time, we're gonna get started. Uh, I see a lot of faces, um gonna run through a short set of updates from leadership then we'll do Q&A. 00:15 Jordan Park: quick note on the agenda, we have product, eng, research, sales, security, people. 00:23 Maya Chen: Cool, Leah you wanna kick us off on product? 00:28 Leah Ortiz: Yeah thanks Maya. So product highlights this quarter, we've been focused on stability and predictability for inference. The big one is Dedicated v2, which is a rework of routing and batching; early pilots show about 18-25% lower p99 latency and 12-17% cost drop in steady-state. These are internal numbers, still polishing. We're planning a pilot with three customers next week. 00:56 Ravi Singh: To add, Dedicated v2 includes a new autoscaler and smarter KV cache invalidation. Note: sometimes the transcription shows K-V cash which, uh, is a little odd. 01:12 Maya Chen: Nice, how about compatibility with Private on-prem installs? 01:18 Samir Kapoor: From research side we've validated the kernel selection improvements across the common op sets. On on-prem it's mostly the same stack, we just expect different perf envelopes depending on GPU families; we'll be publishing a compatibility matrix. 01:34 Leah Ortiz: Also product is shipping a few UX pieces in the console for rollouts: canary controls, per-model usage breakdown, and better tracing. 01:45 Dana Liu: On the commercial side customers are excited. We closed a mid-market renewal this week citing the latency gains. A lot of inbound interest around Dedicated for regulated customers. 01:58 Maya Chen: Great, let's move to ops and reliability. Owen? 02:03 Owen Martinez: We've improved autoscaling stability; fewer spike-related failures this month. We're still watching a networking flake in one EU region; mitigation in place but long term fix in sprint 48. 02:18 Hannah Reed: Security update: SOC2 readiness - we've completed evidence collection for three control categories; remaining gaps are encryption key rotation policies and some tenant isolation audit logs. We're on track for the November remediation window but it's tight, so please prioritize any outstanding doc asks. 02:38 Maya Chen: Carlos, quick finance? 02:41 Carlos Vega: Revenue is pacing to plan, runway unchanged, small reforecast next week for Q1 hiring slippage. 02:50 Maya Chen: Priya, people update? 02:52 Priya Nair: Hiring: we're bringing down open reqs in non-core functions and prioritizing infra and platform engineers. We also are tweaking interview loops to reduce time-to-offer. Retention: voluntary attrition is slightly below benchmark but stay interviews show workload concerns in a few squads, so managers will be flagged. 03:10 Maya Chen: Okay questions? We'll open to chat. 03:13 Unidentified Voice: Hey, can you say more about Dedicated pricing and how it impacts hosted customers? 03:18 Dana Liu: Sure, the model is reserved capacity with burst; hosted remains usage based. The sell is predictable unit costs for enterprise customers who need SLAs. We'll post a spoiler doc with numbers. 03:32 Jordan Park: Technical note - Dedicated v2 supports quantization-friendly execution paths and better batching heuristics; there's a fallback to lighter models for really latency-sensitive traffic. 03:47 Samir Kapoor: On the research side, we've been doing evals tying quality regressions to quantization regimes; initial results show no user-visible regressions for our 8-bit path on most workloads, but we'll continue running regressions. 04:05 Maya Chen: Can we address the SOC2 timeline now? Hannah? 04:09 Hannah Reed: Yes, short answer: still aiming for final attestation next quarter. Immediate ask: engineering to sign off on log retention changes and ops to instrument the tenant audit trails. We'll create a tracker in the security folder. 04:28 Maya Chen: Ok, product question - deployment model choice: hosted vs dedicated vs private: Leah? 04:33 Leah Ortiz: Each has tradeoffs. Hosted is fastest with lower ops for customers. Dedicated is best for predictable throughput and compliance, Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency and air-gapped. The console will keep the same API surface across all three so developers don't have to rewrite client code. 04:55 Unidentified Voice 2: Are we giving customers guidance for quantized models? 04:58 Samir Kapoor: Yes, we have a recommendation set per workload, and Optimize will suggest batching/cache config; we'll publish the first baseline guide next week. 05:12 Maya Chen: A couple housekeeping things: 1) we're pausing a couple non-core projects to focus on launch 2) Q4 OKRs are posted in the handbook, please review. 05:26 Unidentified Voice 3: On the Dedicated pilot - who owns engineering follow-up? 05:30 Ravi Singh: I'll own the pilot engineering coordination, ops and reliability both in the loop. 05:36 Maya Chen: Great, can we get a brief customer highlight? Dana? 05:39 Dana Liu: Yes - a customer in fintech moved from home-grown endpoints to Hosted API, and they're seeing a 2x increase in throughput with 30% lower cost - that's part of the sales case for Dedicated for larger regulated customers. 05:56 Unidentified Voice 4: Any impact from competitors like Bedrock or Anthropic? 05:59 Dana Liu: We see competitive motions, but our differentiation is production economics and observability. We lead with predictable latency and cost controls. 06:10 Maya Chen: OK let's do rapid-fire leadership updates - two bullets each. Jordan? 06:14 Jordan Park: We shipped the kernel picker and the autoscaler; next up is end-to-end perf tests and a public benchmark page. 06:23 Leah Ortiz: Product: rollouts UX, better tracing, and customer feedback loops for evals. 06:29 Samir Kapoor: Research: quantization evals, RLHF experiments for cost reduction, and open-sourcing a small bench harness. 06:37 Ravi Singh: Engineering: focus on Dedicated v2 stabilization, EU networking fix, and reducing incident MTTR. 06:45 Hannah Reed: Security: finish key rotation policy, tenant audit logs, and remediate SOC2 gaps. 06:53 Priya Nair: People: prioritize hires in infra, reduce candidate lead time, and manager coaching on workload balance. 07:02 Maya Chen: Thank you. We'll open to Q&A from the live chat, please drop questions in the Q&A tool. 07:07 Chat Q: Will there be a customer-facing blog about Dedicated v2? 07:10 Leah Ortiz: Yes, marketing and product will co-author a post after the pilot benchmarks land. 07:18 Chat Q: What's the expectation for private/on-prem now? 07:22 Samir Kapoor: On-prem is moving to parity with hosted for core features; still some perf work on older GPUs. 07:33 Maya Chen: We're at about 45 minutes in - thanks for the questions. Final recap: Dedicated v2 pilot next week, security to share gaps, engineering to post perf numbers, people to finalize hiring priorities. 07:49 Maya Chen: Okay that's it - thanks everyone, meeting adjourned. NOTE: Transcript includes typical speech disfluencies and occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., K-V cash, some speaker labels generic).
questions: SOC2 timeline and immediate engineering asks
Dedicated v2 pilot ownership and benchmarks
Private/on-prem feature parity and GPU compatibility
Hiring prioritization for infra and platform
